text.p: The following are leading domestic
stories in Portuguese newspapers.
PUBLICO
- The European Commission wants to study terms of the
so-called Mateus Plan, which is designed to help ailing firms
recover.
- Car assembler AutoEuropa invested 395 billion escudos
until the end of 1996, 58 billion escudos less than expected.
AutoEuropa foresees identical production in 1997, compared to
1996, and the company may only reach capacity production around
2000, AutoEuropa managing director Ralph Rosignolo told the
paper.
- Madeira had a 15.933 billion escudos budget deficit in
1995, 4.641 billion escudos more than in 1994, according to a
report approved by its regional council.
DIARIO DE NOTICIAS
- In Brussels yesterday Portuguese Economy Minister Augusto
Mateus protested against French and German state aid to the
textile and chemical sectors, which he said disrupted
competition inside the European Union.
- Spanish petrol company Cepsa raised its market share to
seven percent from five percent in Portugal by acquiring French
company Elf Aquitaine's petrol stations in Portugal, Cepsa's
managing director in Portugal, Juan Roldan, told the paper.
- The European Commission wants the Portuguese government to
present a new reestructuring plan for loss-making ship repairer
Lisnave.
DIARIO ECONOMICO
- National Statistics Institute national accounts will be
adjusted to conform with those of the Finaance Ministry, an
official source told the paper.
-- Lisbon bureau 3511-3538254
